la:verb:prandeo.gloss: to take or eat breakfast or luncheon, breakfast; to eat (in general)
senses: to take or eat breakfast or luncheon, breakfast; to eat (in general)
to breakfast on, lunch on, take as breakfast or luncheon; to eat (in general)
la:verb:prandeo.html:
prandĕo, di (prandidi, ), sum, 2, v. n. and a.
[prandium].
Neutr., to take breakfast, to breakfast (v. prandium; class.): hic rex cum aceto pransurus est et sale,: prandi in navi,: prandi perbene,: Caninio consule scito neminem prandisse (because he was elected in the afternoon, and resigned his office on the following morning),: sic prandete, commilitones, tamquam apud inferos coenaturi,: ad satietatem,; : prandebat sibi quisque deus,.—
Act., to breakfast on any thing, to take as a breakfast or luncheon; or, in gen., to eat: calidum prandisti prandium,: luscinias prandere,: olus,.—Hence, pransus, a, um, P. a., that has breakfasted (like potus, that has drunk): pransus non avide,; : pransa Lamia,. —Because soldiers were accustomed to eat before an engagement; hence, pransus paratus, or curatus et pransus, of soldiers, fed, i. e. ready, fit for fighting: exercitus pransus, paratus, Cato ap. ; Varr. ap. : ut viri equique curati et pransi essent,: pransus, potus, overfed, gluttonous: adde inscitiam pransi, poti, oscitantis ducis,.
la:verb:prandeo.inflection: di, sum, 2, v. n. and a.

la:noun:prandium.gloss: late breakfast, luncheon, lunch (eaten about midday)
senses: late breakfast, luncheon, lunch (eaten about midday)
la:noun:prandium.html:
prandĭum, ii, n.
Sanscr. prep-, pra-, before; Gr. πρῳην; Dor. πράν, early; and Lat. dies; hence, early in the day, sc. that taken or eaten
,
a late breakfast, luncheon (cf.: jentaculum, cena), usually taken at or soon after noon, composed of bread, fish, cold meats, etc. (it was thought gluttonous to have several dishes and wine at the prandium): ire ad prandium,; : adducere aliquem ad se ad prandium,: coquere alicui prandium,: funus prandio facere,: apparare,to get ready, prepare,: accurare,: ornare,: dare,to give,: obsonare alicui,: anteponere,to set before, serve up,: comedere,: prandere,: in prandio aliquem accipere apud se,: invitare ad prandium,: prandiorum apparatus,; : ad prandium surgere,: panis deinde siccus et sine mensā prandium: post quod non sunt lavendae manus,: post prandium aut cenam bibere volgare est,: de prandio nihil detrahi potuit; paratum fuit non magis hora, nusquam sine caricis, nusquam sine pugillaribus: illae, si panem habeo, propulmentario sunt, si non habeo, pro pane,: prandia cenis usque in lucem ingesta,. The candidates gave such prandia to their tribules, ; the emperor to the people,; ; cf. also ; ; ; ; .—
Transf.
Poet., a meal, in gen.: qui scribit prandia saevi Tereos,.—
The feed or fodder of animals: bubus glandem prandio depromere,: prandio dato ipsis jumentisque eorum,.
